name: Stop feedback pop-ups
summary: Windows will no longer ask you to rate or comment on it.
what: Applies the policy that stops Windows from showing feedback notifications.
benefit: No more interruptions asking for feedback.
risk: None.
advice: Suggested for everyone. You can still send feedback yourself from the Feedback Hub.
facts: Only hides the prompts, it does not change what data is sent
Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every account
Honored on Pro, Enterprise and Education

name: Keep your PC name out of diagnostic data
summary: Stop Windows from adding the name of this PC to diagnostic data.
what: Applies the policy that stops the device name from being included in Windows diagnostic data.
benefit: Your PC name is not attached to what is sent to Microsoft.
risk: None.
advice: Suggested for everyone. It removes one identifying detail at no cost.
facts: Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every account
Honored on Pro, Enterprise and Education

name: Stop the Microsoft configuration download
summary: Windows will not fetch configuration and experiment settings from Microsoft.
what: Applies the policy that stops Windows from connecting to the OneSettings service.
benefit: One less background connection and fewer remote changes to how Windows behaves.
risk: Low. Microsoft cannot switch Windows features on or off remotely, and some diagnostic features get less guidance.
advice: Suggested if you want Windows to stop phoning home for settings. Skip it if you want the newest staged features.
facts: OneSettings is how Microsoft delivers configuration to Windows
Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every account
Honored on Pro, Enterprise and Education

name: Turn off Windows Error Reporting
summary: Stop crash reports from being created and sent.
what: Applies the policy that disables Windows Error Reporting.
benefit: No crash data about your apps leaves the PC and fewer reporting jobs run after a crash.
risk: Low. Microsoft and app makers get no crash reports, and the built in solutions check for known problems stops.
advice: Suggested if you do not want crash data sent. Skip it if you rely on Windows to suggest fixes after a crash.
facts: Crash dumps can contain parts of what was in memory
Does not affect crash dumps you save yourself
Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every account
Honored on Pro, Enterprise and Education

name: Stop speech model downloads
summary: Windows will not download updates to its speech recognition data.
what: Applies the policy that stops automatic updates of speech recognition and speech synthesis models.
benefit: Saves bandwidth and removes one background download.
risk: Low. Speech recognition may be a little less accurate over time.
advice: Suggested if you never use speech features. Safe to skip.
facts: Speech models are data files, not programs
Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every account
Honored on Pro, Enterprise and Education

name: Turn off online speech recognition
summary: Keep your voice from being sent to Microsoft for recognition.
what: Applies the policy that turns off online speech recognition services and hides the switch in Settings.
benefit: Your voice is not sent to cloud speech services.
risk: Low. Voice typing and cloud dictation stop working.
advice: Suggested if you do not use voice typing. Skip it if you dictate.
facts: Applies to cloud speech services only
Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every account
Honored on Pro, Enterprise and Education

name: Stop inking and typing personalization
summary: Windows will not learn from what you type and write.
what: Turns off implicit ink and text collection and contact harvesting for your account.
benefit: Your typing and handwriting are not used to build a personal dictionary.
risk: Low. Autocorrect and suggestions learn less about your words.
advice: Suggested for everyone who wants less data collected about how they type.
facts: These are the values the Settings privacy page writes

name: Stop sending typing data to improve Windows
summary: Turn off the inking and typing improvement program.
what: Sets the per account value that disables sending inking and typing samples to Microsoft.
benefit: Samples of what you type are not sent.
risk: None.
advice: Suggested for everyone.
facts: Does not change the local dictionary

name: Turn off online speech recognition (this account)
summary: Keep your voice from being sent for recognition, for your account only.
what: Sets the per account value that records that you did not accept the online speech privacy statement.
benefit: Your voice is not sent to cloud speech services.
risk: Low. Voice typing and cloud dictation stop working.
advice: Suggested if you do not use voice typing. Works on every edition.
facts: The machine wide policy version needs Pro or higher

name: Never ask for feedback
summary: Set the feedback frequency to Never for your account.
what: Sets the number of feedback requests per period to zero for your account.
benefit: Windows does not ask you for feedback.
risk: None.
advice: Suggested for everyone. Works on every edition.
facts: This is the Never choice in Settings, Privacy and security, Diagnostics and feedback

name: Stop saving search history
summary: Windows will not remember what you searched for on this device or in your account.
what: Turns off device search history and cloud content search for Microsoft and work or school accounts.
benefit: Searches are not stored and cloud files are not searched from Windows search.
risk: Low. Search no longer suggests your past searches or finds cloud only files.
advice: Suggested for everyone who wants a private search box.
facts: Covers device history and both cloud search switches
These are the values the Settings search permissions page writes

name: Turn off Cortana
summary: Block Cortana with a policy.
what: Applies the policy that disallows Cortana.
benefit: Cortana cannot run or collect searches on builds that still include it.
risk: None.
advice: Suggested for older builds that still ship Cortana. Current Windows 11 builds no longer include the standalone app.
facts: Cortana as a separate app has been retired
Mainly useful on older Windows builds
Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every account
Honored on Pro, Enterprise and Education

name: Block Cortana on the lock screen
summary: Stop Cortana from answering while the PC is locked.
what: Applies the policy that disallows Cortana above the lock screen.
benefit: Nobody can use Cortana without signing in.
risk: None.
advice: Suggested for older builds that still ship Cortana.
facts: Cortana as a separate app has been retired
Mainly useful on older Windows builds
Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every account
Honored on Pro, Enterprise and Education

name: Keep search from using your location
summary: Stop Windows search from using where you are.
what: Applies the policy that stops search from using location information.
benefit: Search results are not tailored to your location.
risk: None.
advice: Suggested for everyone.
facts: Does not turn off location for apps
Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every account
Honored on Pro, Enterprise and Education

name: Keep search on this PC
summary: Stop Windows search from looking in cloud sources like OneDrive and SharePoint.
what: Sets the Windows Search policy that disallows cloud search.
benefit: Search only looks at this PC.
risk: Low. Files that exist only in the cloud are not found from the search box.
advice: Suggested if you do not search cloud files from Windows. Skip it if you do.
facts: Applies to the search box and Start search
Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every account
Honored on Pro, Enterprise and Education

name: Hide search highlights
summary: Remove the daily pictures and trending items from the search box.
what: Sets the Windows Search policy that turns off search highlights.
benefit: A plain search box with no trending content or tracking of what you click.
risk: None.
advice: Suggested for everyone who finds the highlights distracting.
facts: Applies to the search box and search home
Needs a Windows build with search highlights
Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every account
Honored on Pro, Enterprise and Education

name: No web results in search (all accounts)
summary: Stop Windows search from querying the web.
what: Sets the Windows Search policy that disables web queries and web results.
benefit: Nothing you type in search is sent to the web.
risk: Low. Search shows only results from this PC.
advice: Suggested on Enterprise and Education. On Home and Pro use the per account version.
facts: Windows honors this policy on Enterprise and Education only

name: Turn off Windows tips
summary: Stop Windows from showing tips, tricks and suggestions.
what: Applies the policy that turns off Windows tips.
benefit: No tip pop-ups or notifications that push features.
risk: None.
advice: Suggested on Enterprise and Education. On Home and Pro use the per account suggestions switch.
facts: Windows honors this policy on Enterprise and Education only

name: Turn off Windows Spotlight everywhere
summary: Remove Spotlight pictures, tips and suggestions from the lock screen, desktop and Settings.
what: Applies the Spotlight policies for the lock screen, desktop, Settings, notifications and the welcome experience.
benefit: No rotating pictures with promotional tips, and no Spotlight content in Settings.
risk: Low. The lock screen uses a fixed picture instead of Spotlight.
advice: Suggested on Enterprise and Education. On Home and Pro use the lock screen switch below.
facts: Windows honors these policies on Enterprise and Education only

name: No third party suggestions in Spotlight
summary: Stop Windows from suggesting other companies content.
what: Applies the per account policy that stops third party content suggestions.
benefit: No ads for other companies apps and services in Spotlight.
risk: None.
advice: Suggested for everyone on Pro and above.
facts: Honored on Pro, Enterprise and Education

name: No Spotlight or tips on the lock screen
summary: Stop the rotating lock screen pictures and tips for your account.
what: Turns off the rotating lock screen and its tips for your account.
benefit: The lock screen stays a plain picture with no promotions.
risk: None.
advice: Suggested for everyone. Works on every edition.
facts: These are the values Settings writes when you leave Spotlight

name: Stop online tips in Settings
summary: The Settings app will not fetch tips and help from Microsoft.
what: Applies the policy that stops Settings from retrieving online tips and help content.
benefit: Settings works offline and does not contact Microsoft for tips.
risk: None.
advice: Suggested for everyone.
facts: Settings pages still work as before
Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every account
Honored on Pro, Enterprise and Education

name: Hide promotions in File Explorer
summary: Stop sync provider notices and offers inside File Explorer.
what: Turns off sync provider notifications in File Explorer for your account.
benefit: No OneDrive and Microsoft 365 offers in the folder view.
risk: None.
advice: Suggested for everyone. Works on every edition.

name: Hide Start recommendations
summary: Remove tips, shortcuts and suggested apps from the Start menu.
what: Turns off recommendations and account notices in the Start menu for your account.
benefit: A cleaner Start menu without suggested apps and promotions.
risk: None.
advice: Suggested for everyone. Windows 11 only.

name: Stop tracking which apps you launch
summary: Windows will not record the apps you open to improve Start.
what: Turns off app launch tracking for your account.
benefit: Start does not keep a list of the apps you use most.
risk: Low. The most used apps list in Start stays empty.
advice: Suggested for everyone who wants less activity tracking.

name: Hide recent files and frequent folders
summary: Stop showing and tracking recently opened items.
what: Turns off recent item tracking in Start, jump lists and File Explorer for your account.
benefit: Nobody sees what you opened lately by looking at Start or Quick access.
risk: Low. Recent lists and jump lists stay empty.
advice: Suggested on shared PCs and for privacy. Skip it if you use the recent lists a lot.
facts: Clears nothing that is already saved

name: Stop syncing settings to the cloud
summary: Windows will not sync your settings, themes and passwords between PCs.
what: Applies the policy that turns off Sync your settings and locks the switch.
benefit: Your preferences and passwords are not uploaded.
risk: Low. A new PC does not get your theme and settings automatically.
advice: Suggested if you do not want settings stored in your Microsoft account. Skip it if you use several PCs.
facts: Covers themes, passwords, language, accessibility and other Windows settings
Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every account
Honored on Pro, Enterprise and Education

name: Stop syncing the clipboard across devices
summary: What you copy stays on this PC.
what: Applies the policy that stops clipboard contents from being synced to other devices.
benefit: Passwords and text you copy are not sent to the cloud.
risk: None.
advice: Suggested for everyone. You can still copy and paste on this PC.
facts: Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every account
Honored on Pro, Enterprise and Education

name: Turn off clipboard history
summary: Windows will not keep a list of what you copied.
what: Applies the policy that stops the history of clipboard contents from being stored.
benefit: Old copied text and images are not kept in memory.
risk: Low. The Win+V history list stays empty.
advice: Suggested if you copy passwords or private text. Skip it if you use Win+V.
facts: Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every account
Honored on Pro, Enterprise and Education

name: Stop cloud backup of text messages
summary: Cellular text messages are not backed up to Microsoft.
what: Applies the policy that stops message backup and restore through Microsoft cloud services.
benefit: Your messages are not stored in the cloud.
risk: Low. You cannot restore messages from the cloud.
advice: Suggested for almost everyone. Only matters on PCs with cellular messaging.
facts: Only affects PCs that handle cellular text messages
Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every account
Honored on Pro, Enterprise and Education

name: Turn off Find My Device
summary: Stop registering this PC and its location in the cloud.
what: Applies the policy that turns Find My Device off.
benefit: Your PC location is not stored in your Microsoft account.
risk: Low. You cannot locate this PC from account.microsoft.com if it is lost.
advice: Suggested for desktops that stay at home. Skip it on laptops you could lose.
facts: Also removes the last location stored in the cloud for active pens
Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every account
Honored on Pro, Enterprise and Education

name: Turn off Phone link
summary: Stop this PC from linking to a phone.
what: Applies the policy that turns off phone and PC linking.
benefit: No continuing tasks from a phone and no phone data synced to this PC.
risk: Low. Phone Link and Continue on PC stop working.
advice: Suggested if you never link a phone. Skip it if you do.
facts: Applies to linking a phone with this PC
Enforced by a machine policy, so it applies to every account
Honored on Pro, Enterprise and Education

name: Block the lock screen camera
summary: The camera cannot be started from the lock screen.
what: Applies the policy that prevents enabling the lock screen camera.
benefit: Nobody can open the camera without signing in.
risk: None.
advice: Suggested for tablets and shared PCs. Safe to skip on a desktop.
facts: Hides the switch in Settings too

name: Hide app notifications on the lock screen
summary: Notifications do not show while the PC is locked.
what: Applies the policy that turns off app notifications on the lock screen.
benefit: Nobody can read your messages without signing in.
risk: Low. You will not see notifications until you sign in.
advice: Suggested for laptops and shared PCs.

name: Turn off Widgets
summary: Remove the Widgets board and its taskbar button.
what: Applies the policy that disallows the widgets feature, including content on the taskbar.
benefit: No news feed in the taskbar and one less background process.
risk: None.
advice: Suggested for everyone who does not read the Widgets board.
facts: Applies to the whole widgets experience

name: Hide the Chat button
summary: Remove the Chat (Teams) button from the taskbar.
what: Hides the taskbar Chat button for your account.
benefit: More room on the taskbar.
risk: None.
advice: Suggested if you do not use Chat. Newer builds no longer show it.

name: Hide the Copilot button
summary: Remove the Copilot button from the taskbar.
what: Hides the taskbar Copilot button for your account.
benefit: More room on the taskbar.
risk: None.
advice: Suggested if you do not use Copilot.
facts: Hides the button only, it does not remove the app

name: Turn off Recall snapshots
summary: Windows will not save snapshots of your screen for Recall.
what: Applies the policy that turns off saving snapshots for use with Recall. Snapshots saved earlier are deleted when it is enabled.
benefit: Nothing on your screen is recorded for later search.
risk: Low. Recall has nothing to search.
advice: Suggested for everyone who does not want a searchable record of what was on screen.
facts: Deletes snapshots that were saved earlier
Needs Windows 11 24H2 with the Recall update

name: Make Recall unavailable
summary: Remove the Recall component so nobody can turn it on.
what: Applies the policy that disables the Recall component. Windows removes its files and deletes saved snapshots, and needs a restart.
benefit: Recall cannot be enabled by anyone on this PC.
risk: Low. Recall is gone until you revert and restart.
advice: Suggested if you never want Recall on this PC. Skip it if you might try it later.
facts: Needs Windows 11 24H2 with the Recall update

name: Turn off the Copilot pane
summary: Block the older Copilot in Windows pane with a policy.
what: Applies the per account policy that turns off Windows Copilot and removes its taskbar icon.
benefit: Copilot cannot be opened from the taskbar on builds that include the pane.
risk: None.
advice: Suggested if you do not use Copilot. The policy is marked deprecated and applies to the older pane only.
facts: Deprecated by Microsoft in favor of removing the app
Does not affect the newer Copilot app

name: Turn off Paint image creation tools
summary: Disable Cocreator, generative fill and Image Creator in Paint.
what: Applies the three Paint policies that disable these features.
benefit: Paint works as a plain editor and sends nothing to online image services.
risk: None.
advice: Suggested if you do not use these tools.

name: Stop sharing detections with Microsoft MAPS
summary: Keep Microsoft Defender from sending data to the Microsoft cloud protection service.
what: Applies the Defender policy that leaves Microsoft MAPS. Real time protection and local scanning stay on.
benefit: Less data about files and detections is sent to Microsoft.
risk: Medium. Cloud protection reacts more slowly to brand new threats.
advice: Suggested only if privacy matters more than the fastest protection against new threats. Skip it if Defender is your only antivirus.
facts: Cloud delivered protection finds new threats faster
Windows Security may show the setting as managed

name: Never send file samples to Microsoft
summary: Defender will not upload suspicious files for analysis.
what: Applies the Defender policy that sends no file samples.
benefit: Your files are never uploaded by Defender.
risk: Low. Defender cannot ask the cloud to analyze unknown files.
advice: Suggested if you handle private documents. Skip it if you want the strongest cloud checks.
facts: Windows Security may show the setting as managed

name: Turn off Game Bar recording
summary: Stop background game recording and broadcasting for your account.
what: Turns off Game DVR background capture for your account.
benefit: No background recording costs performance or disk space.
risk: Low. Game Bar clips and the record last 30 seconds feature stop working.
advice: Suggested if you do not record gameplay. Skip it if you use Game Bar clips.
facts: Game Bar can still open with Win+G

name: Turn on Game Mode
summary: Let Windows favor games when one is running.
what: Turns on Game Mode for your account.
benefit: Windows reduces background work while a game is in focus, which can steady frame rates on busy PCs.
risk: None.
advice: Suggested for gaming PCs. The effect is small on powerful hardware.
facts: Gains vary by game and PC

name: Hardware accelerated GPU scheduling
summary: Let the graphics card manage its own memory scheduling.
what: Turns on hardware accelerated GPU scheduling. It only has an effect on a supported graphics card and driver.
benefit: Can lower latency in some games and enable features such as frame generation.
risk: Low. A few games or drivers run worse with it on. Needs a restart.
advice: Suggested on current NVIDIA, AMD or Intel cards if a game or feature asks for it. Skip it if your games already run well.
facts: Needs a supported graphics card and driver

name: Turn off AutoPlay
summary: Stop Windows from acting on drives and discs when you connect them.
what: Turns off AutoPlay for all media and devices for your account.
benefit: A USB stick cannot start something by itself or pop up choices. It closes a common way to spread malware.
risk: None.
advice: Suggested for everyone.
facts: You can still open the drive from File Explorer

name: Turn off Remote Assistance
summary: Block people from being invited to control this PC.
what: Applies the policies that turn off solicited and unsolicited Remote Assistance.
benefit: Nobody can connect to this PC through Remote Assistance.
risk: Low. You cannot invite someone to help you remotely this way.
advice: Suggested unless you use Remote Assistance to get help.
facts: Does not affect Quick Assist or Remote Desktop
